decision.title: Use speech-native-builder soul for terminal-native VCS work
decision.summary: The active project soul is speech-native-builder. Future agents should preserve terminal-native speech capture, visible device/listening state, live transcript output, stable visual context ids, and honest constraint reporting.
decision.impact: New sessions should read SOUL.md and AGENTS.md before implementation, run gad snapshot, and avoid browser/web surfaces for core terminal workflows unless explicitly approved.

decision.title: Adopt Dr. Stein as the project-specific SLM soul
decision.summary: The active slm_learning soul is Dr. Stein, a mad scientist responsible for creating SLMs, souls, and reasoning loops from this project itself. Gilgamesh remains the broader/default leader, but Dr. Stein governs project-specific terminal lab behavior.
decision.impact: Future sessions should read SOUL.md and narrative/souls/dr-stein.md, preserve terminal-native speech/VCS constraints, and treat the menu shell as a chat/composer lab interface for lessons and self-improvement.

decision.title: Adopt MoE and Network Morphism for Extensible Architecture
decision.summary: Upgraded the MiniLlama architecture to support Mixture of Experts (MoE) routing and Progressive Network Growing (Network Morphism). This allows the SLM to grow capacity dynamically without catastrophic forgetting.
decision.impact: Future fine-tuning loops will target moe_model.pt or grown_model.pt to leverage specialized reasoning experts.

decision.title: Implement MLOps and bfloat16 Quantization
decision.summary: Implemented a strict MLOps pipeline to compress all .pt checkpoints from fp32 to bfloat16, cutting disk usage by 50% with zero accuracy loss, preventing local storage exhaustion.
decision.impact: All future models saved must use bfloat16 or be swept by the mlops_manager script.

decision.title: Enforce Domain Constraining for Fluid Intelligence
decision.summary: Established gad_supported_stacks.json to strictly prune unblessed frameworks (e.g., Svelte, Vue) from the training corpus. This starves the SLM of irrelevant crystallized knowledge, freeing parameter capacity for pure reasoning and Next.js mastery.
decision.impact: The monorepo ingestion pipeline strictly filters files based on this registry. Future dataset generation must obey these bounds.

decision.title: Multi-Point Progressive Network Growth
decision.summary: Upgraded Network Morphism from single-point layer append to multi-point insertion with strategy-guided placement (uniform/early/late/middle). New identity layers are inserted at computed positions across the network so each learns features appropriate to its depth: syntax (early), semantics (middle), or reasoning (late).
decision.impact: The --strategy flag controls growth direction. Future evolution cycles should use 'uniform' for general capacity, 'late' for reasoning, 'early' for syntax understanding.

decision.title: Context Window Strategy: Flush + Reprocess on Model Swap
decision.summary: When hot-swapping between Kael and Dr. Stein mid-conversation, the KV-cache is invalidated because K/V tensors are weight-dependent. Current strategy: flush cache and reprocess full history through the new model. Future: shared base weights + LoRA adapter swap to preserve KV-cache.
decision.impact: Model swaps cost O(history_length) compute. For long conversations, this may introduce latency on swap. The LoRA path eliminates this cost entirely.

decision.title: Refactor TUI to Single-Responsibility Components
decision.summary: Dismantled the monolithic chat_screen.py into slash_commands.py (command parsing), model_runner.py (model lifecycle + context window), and telemetry.py (GAD observability). chat_screen.py is now purely a UI orchestrator.
decision.impact: Future TUI changes must respect the component boundary. Model logic goes in model_runner, command parsing in slash_commands, logging in telemetry. chat_screen only composes UI.

decision.title: Align with Frontier Architecture: System Prompts + Full Fine-Tuning, Not LoRA Swapping
decision.summary:
Frontier models (Claude Opus, GPT-5.5, Gemini) do NOT swap weights at runtime. Persona differences (Kael vs Dr. Stein) are handled via system prompt injection into the context window — no weight modifications at inference time. Domain knowledge is baked in during training via SFT and RLHF/DPO, not adapter swapping. LoRA is reserved for future consumer extensibility (users specializing Dr. Stein for their specific project without full retraining). This supersedes the LoRA-swap assumption in decision slm-learning-008; the KV-cache invalidation problem is moot because we no longer swap weights mid-conversation.
Training pipeline for Dr. Stein alignment: 1. Pre-training (SmolLM2 base — already done) 2. SFT on monorepo corpus (scripts/09_finetune_dr_stein.py) 3. Future: DPO preference optimization for judgment/quality
decision.impact: Kael and Dr. Stein MUST share the exact same base checkpoint. The only runtime difference is the system prompt. Fine-tuning produces one shared checkpoint, not separate per-persona weights. LoRA adapters are a consumer-facing feature, not an internal architecture mechanism.

decision.title: VRAM ceiling = 6GB GTX 1660 Ti — every model must load on baseline GPU
decision.summary: Operating constraint: every checkpoint, training run, and inference path must fit on the 6GB GTX 1660 Ti baseline. Drives architecture, batch size, and quantization choices. Larger memory available via the recently-attached Razer Core eGPU (second 1660 Ti, currently not detected by torch — needs Thunderbolt/eGPU driver verification before counting on it) but baseline assumption stays single-6GB so artifacts remain useful on a single dev box.
decision.impact: Forces PEFT/LoRA/QLoRA over full fine-tunes for any model larger than ~200M params; constrains MoE expert size; rules out 7B-class models locally without aggressive 4-bit quantization.

decision.title: Adopt Hugging Face datasets ecosystem (FineWeb, The Stack, OpenMathInstruct, OpenCodeReasoning, FineMath)
decision.summary: Move beyond hand-curated + monorepo-only training data. Adopt datasets.load_dataset() pipeline for: code (The Stack / OpenCodeReasoning), math (OpenMathInstruct, FineMath), general reasoning (OpenMathReasoning, synthetic mixes), web text (FineWeb). Existing hand-curated GAD-tool seed remains canonical for tool-call distillation; HF corpora cover code/math/reasoning tracks the model has never seen.
decision.impact: Adds datasets dependency; need streaming + on-the-fly tokenization to avoid downloading TBs; enables Stage 2.5+ to fine-tune on real code/math distributions instead of monorepo text.

decision.title: Use TRL SFTTrainer + PEFT (LoRA/QLoRA) for fine-tuning, not bespoke training loops
decision.summary: Stop rolling our own training loops in scripts/16_reasoning_training.py / 17_dpo_training.py for new tracks. For Stage 2.5 GAD-tool fine-tune and all subsequent fine-tunes, adopt the trl SFTTrainer + peft LoRA stack. QLoRA (4-bit base + LoRA adapters) is the only realistic path to fitting larger checkpoints on a 6GB GPU. Existing scripts 09/16/17 remain for the from-scratch educational track but are not the path forward for scaling.
decision.impact: Adds trl, peft, bitsandbytes dependencies. Faster iteration, smaller checkpoints (LoRA adapters are KB-MB), proven optimizer/scheduler defaults. Loss of the 'transparent from-scratch' framing for new code, but that's a deliberate trade for getting actual results.

decision.title: Iterative train/prune/retrain loop — keep only most relevant weights, optimize for fluid intelligence
decision.summary: Adopt the iterative train -> magnitude/movement-prune -> retrain -> prune cycle as the core SLM development loop. Goal: a small model with high reasoning per parameter, NOT a model packed with crystallized knowledge. The bet is that reasoning quality beats memorized facts for our use case (GAD operator + project context + tool-call generation). Output may be slower per token but should be reliably correct. This is the explicit tradeoff for competing against frontier models locally.
decision.impact: New scripts: prune_checkpoint.py (magnitude/movement), retrain_after_prune.py. Pruning ratio + retrain epochs become first-class hyperparameters in experiments/configs/. Eval matrix gets a 'sparsity' column.

decision.title: MoE with reasoning-specialized experts as the long-term architecture
decision.summary: Confirms direction set in slm-learning-004 (MoE) but narrows the experts: each expert is shaped for a reasoning-heavy domain (math chain-of-thought, code synthesis, GAD-tool routing, planning-doc parsing). Top-K router with K small. The bet: many small reasoning-specialized experts beat one wide generalist at the same total param count, and matches the VRAM ceiling because only K experts activate per token.
decision.impact: Architecture work: MoE upcycling from dense Stage 2.5 checkpoint. Router training becomes its own track. Capacity factor tuning. Per-expert eval (which expert fires on which prompt class) becomes a new instrumentation axis.

decision.title: Free remote compute (Colab/Kaggle/HF Spaces) for training; local stays for inference + planning
decision.summary: When training jobs exceed local 6GB GPU + reasonable wall-time budget, push the job to free-tier Colab (T4/A100), Kaggle (P100/T4 x2), or HF Spaces. Inference, evaluation, and planning stay local for privacy + iteration speed. Establish a 'remote training' workflow: package a config + dataset URI, generate a notebook/launcher script, push, retrieve checkpoint, log result back into experiments/INDEX.md as if it were a local run. Compute policy memory already permits this.
decision.impact: New scripts: scripts/remote/colab_launcher.py, kaggle_launcher.py. Need HF Hub account for checkpoint upload. CI / experiment manifest gets 'compute_target' field (local|colab|kaggle|hf-spaces|hf-hub-train).

decision.title: Synthetic data generation via stronger LLMs as a first-class data-augmentation track
decision.summary: Beyond paraphrase distillation (Claude-haiku-4-5 teacher), adopt synthetic-reasoning-trace generation: prompt a stronger model (Claude Opus, Sonnet, or external) to produce step-by-step reasoning chains for a problem, filter for quality (model-graded + human spot-check), and mix with real data. Tools: DeepEval synthetic_data, EvidentlyAI, or custom prompts. Mirror the 'frontier bootstrapping' pattern at our scale.
decision.impact: New scripts: scripts/synth_reasoning_traces.py. Quality-filter + dedup pipeline. Cost lives on Anthropic API; track $ per 1K filtered pairs.

decision.title: High reasoning > crystallized knowledge as the explicit competing-with-frontier strategy
decision.summary: Strategy: a small model with strong fluid intelligence and adaptability beats a small model with memorized facts. Output may be slower per token (more reasoning steps) but should be reliably correct. This mirrors the GAD context framework / ecosystem 'survival skills' pattern: durability via reasoning over context lookups, not via baked-in knowledge. All training data, eval design, and architecture choices should favor reasoning capacity over knowledge capacity.
decision.impact: Reasoning-step datasets (OpenMathReasoning, OpenCodeReasoning, synthetic CoT traces) outweigh raw-text corpora in the data mix. Eval suites need reasoning-quality scoring (intermediate-step correctness) not just final-answer match. Architecture leans toward more attention heads, deeper FFN, longer effective context (RoPE scaling).

decision.title: Distillation runs through Claude Code subagent dispatch, NOT Anthropic API key
decision.summary: Per user preference 2026-05-05: SLM distillation pairs are produced by spawning a Claude subagent inside Claude Code (Agent tool with subagent_type=general-purpose or claude-haiku-4-5 explicit), not by calling the Anthropic API directly with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The orchestrating Claude session collects responses and writes them into data/distilled_pairs.jsonl. scripts/distill_gad_pairs.py kept as documentation of the contract but the live path is subagent dispatch.
decision.impact: No API key plumbing in this project. Distillation cadence is bound to interactive Claude Code sessions (or scheduled /loop runs). Effectively free for the user; trivially adjustable model selection per call.

decision.title: Multi-GPU strategy: local + remote split via per-config compute_target
decision.summary: Multi-GPU sharding is split between local (GTX 1660 Ti #0, optionally eGPU #1 once detected) and remote (Colab T4/A100, Kaggle P100/T4x2, HF Spaces). Each FinetuneConfig grows a 'compute_target' field: local-cuda-0 / local-cuda-1 / colab-t4 / colab-a100 / kaggle-t4x2 / hf-spaces. Sweep runner dispatches each config to its target. Local jobs run via subprocess + CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; remote jobs render to a notebook + dataset URI, push, retrieve checkpoint, log into INDEX.md as if local. Manifest schema stays portable across targets.
decision.impact: FinetuneConfig + sweep_finetune.py both extended. New scripts/remote/{colab,kaggle,hf}_launcher.py. Network IO + HF Hub auth become real concerns.

decision.title: North-star training target: model can scaffold a 'gad site'-quality landing page with minimal prompting
decision.summary: Concrete bar for 'this model can actually code': asked to create a landing site for any GAD project, the SLM should produce something visually + structurally comparable to the gad site that ships with every GAD project (Next.js scaffold with project home / requirements / phases / decisions / docs nav). Doesn't need to be byte-identical — needs to be the same class of artifact with little hand-holding. This is the explicit benchmark for whether the reasoning-over-knowledge bet (slm-learning-018) is paying off.
decision.impact: Training data tracks now include: (1) gad site source as code distillation pairs, (2) Next.js + Tailwind component patterns from FineWeb / The Stack, (3) synthetic 'scaffold-this-page' tasks via Claude subagent. New eval: structural diff between model output and a reference gad-site scaffold (file presence, route shape, component nesting). When a checkpoint passes 70% structural-diff coverage, the bet is validated.

decision.title: Adopt DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B as primary local reas...
decision.summary: Adopt DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B as primary local reasoning base; Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct as instruction-following control. Both fit fp16 inference on 1660 Ti (~3GB). Same Qwen tokenizer family, drop-in for current LoRA target_modules. Run as parallel sweep on the 153 GAD-tool pairs to get apples-to-apples comparison instead of guessing which 1.5B fits the GAD-CLI translation task best.

decision.title: HF Hub for adapter storage (public repos for cost).
decision.summary: HF Hub for adapter storage (public repos for cost). Push adapter dirs after each Stage 2.5 run via huggingface_hub library; full base models stay on HF and are re-downloaded on demand. Mirror local + remote; nothing lost if local disk dies. CLI: use new 'hf' binary at ~/.local/bin/hf; library calls work from any venv with huggingface_hub installed.

decision.title: Empirical: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B underperforms Qw...
decision.summary: Empirical: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B underperforms Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on the CLI/instruction-following track. First sweep results: control 22/30 (73.3%) GAD-tools, distill 8/30 (26.7%); distill 0/10 HumanEval (every gen unterminated <think> -> SyntaxError); distill 5/50 GSM8K (same as random baseline). The distill model's reasoning traces are useful but at max_new_tokens=50-200 they get truncated mid-thought. Decision: distill artifact stays as a separate REASONING-track candidate with max_new_tokens>=1024, not retired. Not part of the CLI sweep going forward. Both adapters published at scrubster/dr-stein-stage25-qwen15-instruct-control and scrubster/dr-stein-stage25-qwen15-distill-reasoning.

decision.title: Empirical reversal: bf16 trains 3.2x faster than fp16 on ...
decision.summary: Empirical reversal: bf16 trains 3.2x faster than fp16 on GTX 1660 Ti for Stage 2.5 LoRA fine-tunes via TRL SFTTrainer. A/B at 2026-05-05 with identical Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct config + same seed: fp16 = 768.9s, bf16 = 240.0s, both 22/30 GAD-tools. Theoretical claim that Turing's lack of native BF16 tensor cores would make bf16 slower (slm-learning-022 addendum) was wrong — TRL's fp16 path adds GradScaler/autocast overhead that exceeds bf16's slower matmul. Default for all Turing local training: bf16=true. Configs updated. Confidence: high (single A/B, deterministic seed, identical eval). Re-test if TRL or PEFT major-version changes.

decision.title: Empirical: vocab-anchored distillation (canonical gad CLI...
decision.summary: Empirical: vocab-anchored distillation (canonical gad CLI surface + Haiku 4.5 subagent + 8 known failure-mode reinforcement) closes the 22/30 -> 30/30 gap on GAD-tools eval. 5x training data with single-variable change (more+better data, not paraphrase) eliminated all v1 vocabulary hallucinations. Method generalizes: when target output domain has a finite canonical surface, walk the surface, distill against it, train. CLI-track is solved at the current eval scale; expand the eval to 100+ harder cases or move on. Math/code tracks still 0%/4% - distinct skill, distinct data needed.

decision.title: Empirical: fine-tuning a reasoning-distilled model (DeepS...
decision.summary: Empirical: fine-tuning a reasoning-distilled model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) on terse single-line CLI commands DESTROYS its <think> reasoning structure. Tested at max_new_tokens=2048: distill adapter still produced 0/8 on HumanEval (killed at 8/10) with identical SyntaxError-on-unterminated-string pattern as the 128-token run. The model lost its ability to terminate <think> blocks coherently. Lesson: don't fine-tune a reasoning model on non-reasoning data — separate adapters for separate skills (slm-learning-024 confirmed). Math/code track now uses Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (not the distill base) + OpenMathInstruct-2 data per slm-learning-012.

decision.title: Pivot all training to Colab Pro (A100).
decision.summary: Pivot all training to Colab Pro (A100). Local 1660 Ti hit hard ceiling: bs=1 only feasible config for any 1.5B+ base, segfault-on-second-process pattern unfixable, 4.7h wall times kill iteration. Colab Pro at $10/mo gives A100 access (~10-15x faster), 24h runtimes, easy reconnect. notebooks/train_colab.ipynb is the entrypoint — user opens, attaches A100, runs all. Three first-batch configs in experiments/configs/colab/: qwen15_math_5k, qwen3b_v2_cli, qwen3b_math_5k. Adapters auto-publish to scrubster/dr-stein-*. Inference + planning stay local per project_compute_policy.md. Future RunPod pivot if longer runs needed (>24h) or specific GPU.

decision.title: GAD-tools 30-case eval is SATURATED at the 1.5B+ level.
decision.summary: GAD-tools 30-case eval is SATURATED at the 1.5B+ level. Empirical: Qwen2.5-1.5B+783 vocab pairs = 30/30 (v2). Qwen2.5-3B+same data = 30/30 (colab-qwen3b-v2-cli) in 213s training. Bigger base does NOT lift this metric because the metric ceiling is already met. To differentiate model capability above 30/30 we need: (a) harder eval set with edge cases and complex multi-flag commands, OR (b) eval on tasks beyond CLI translation (HumanEval, GSM8K, full coding agent tasks). Direct implication: stop scaling base size for the CLI track; further investments should target other tracks (math, code, tool-use) or eval expansion.

decision.title: GAD competitive thesis (defensible claim): A GAD-orchestr...
decision.summary: GAD competitive thesis (defensible claim): A GAD-orchestrated system with durable context, repo-specific memory, tools, tests, routing, eval pressure, and specialist SLMs can beat a bare frontier model on bounded workflows inside our ecosystem. We do NOT compete by trying to out-pretrain frontier — they have scale, RL, long-context training, and trillions of tokens we cannot match. We compete on leverage: domain specificity, durable state, tool harness, routing economics, ensemble verification. Validation: game-task A/B/C eval (bare Opus vs Opus+GAD vs Opus+GAD+specialists) on bounded tasks with unit-test scoring.

decision.title: Router-first economic core.
decision.summary: Router-first economic core. Architecture: input -> cheap classical ML classifier (logistic/SVM/XGBoost on text features + repo metadata) -> specialist SLM OR frontier runtime. Use classical ML for routing/triage/anomaly because it is cheap, deterministic, inspectable, fast. Use SLMs/LLMs for generation only. The router is the unlock that makes small specialists economically viable; without routing, specialists are dead weight. Cost target: router decision in <1ms at zero GPU cost.

decision.title: Model evolution ladder + bake-only-behind-promotion-gate.
decision.summary: Model evolution ladder + bake-only-behind-promotion-gate. Sequence: specialist LoRA -> stacked adapter experiment -> multi-task LoRA -> bake candidate -> regression suite -> promoted GAD base -> new specialist layer on top. Bake (merge_and_unload) is PERMANENT and risks catastrophic forgetting; only allowed after passing 7-criterion promotion gate: (1) GAD CLI eval >= prior, (2) tool-call JSON validity >70%, (3) held-out trace prediction, (4) unit-test repair task pass rate, (5) game feature A/B/C eval, (6) regression against all prior skill specialists, (7) cost/latency measurement. Use PEFT TIES/DARE/SVD merging utilities for multi-LoRA merges (safer than naive sum).

decision.title: Tracked techniques registry.
decision.summary: Tracked techniques registry. Active in our experiment ladder: LoRA (cheap per-skill, current default), QLoRA (next: 7B-32B fine-tunes on limited cloud budget), DoRA (try when LoRA underfits — magnitude+direction decomposition), LoRA+ (separate LRs for A/B matrices, ~2x speedup), TIES/DARE (multi-LoRA merging), DPO/ORPO (preference training after SFT — ORPO is reference-model-free), execution-driven RL (long-term: unit tests as reward signal), speculative decoding (1.5B drafter + 7B verifier for inference latency), KV/prefix caching (reuse GAD context blocks across requests), classical ML (SVM/logistic/XGBoost for router/risk/eval-triage). Each technique has status: not-yet-tried / experimental / canonical / abandoned-because. Living registry in .planning/notes/2026-05-06-techniques-registry.md.

decision.title: Tool-use Tier 1 model is the highest-leverage training ta...
decision.summary: Tool-use Tier 1 model is the highest-leverage training target. Inputs: real Claude-Code-on-this-repo trace events (.planning/.trace-events.jsonl, 974 events, 4 sessions, secret-redacted). 780 (instruction, command) pairs extracted via scripts/extract_tool_use_pairs.py. Plan: (1) sanity-train Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct LoRA (currently running, job 69facbbeb745af80fb37395d), (2) if loss converges + tool-name accuracy >50% on held-out, graduate to (3) Qwen2.5-Coder-7B + QLoRA on same data + supplemental traces. Why coder base: tool-use is fundamentally code-call shaped — repo state + intent -> tool name + JSON args is a code-prediction task. Gate before 7B run: 1.5B sanity must pass.

decision.title: Empirical: math training on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct + 5000 ...
decision.summary: Empirical: math training on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct + 5000 OpenMathInstruct-2 pairs lifts GSM8K from 2/50 (4%) to 25/50 (50%) — 12x. Cost: $0.16 on HF Jobs L4. Validates that small specialist LoRAs achieve significant lift on narrow tasks with modest data. Caveat: 3B base with SAME recipe scored only 14/50 (undertrained — bigger model needs more epochs/data). Implication for ladder: the 5k+2-epoch recipe is right for 1.5B; for 3B+ scale to 3-5 epochs OR 10-20k pairs. Tooluse sanity train (Qwen2.5-1.5B + 780 trace pairs) converged cleanly (loss 0.39, token acc 90%). Tier 1 7B coder run (SL-T-04-06) is unblocked — sanity gate from slm-learning-034 passes.

decision.title: Two-tier routing architecture decided.
decision.summary: Two-tier routing architecture decided. Layer 1: Runtime router (SL-T-04-08) — classical ML classifier picks Claude Code / Codex CLI / Gemini CLI / OpenCode / frontier-API per task. Layer 2: Agent router (SL-T-04-01) — within a runtime, picks which subagent (gad-planner, gad-executor, gad-doc-verifier, etc.) for a sub-step. Layer 3: Tool router — within an agent, picks gad CLI command (already validated by v2 30/30). Each layer is classical ML where possible (cheap, deterministic, debuggable per slm-learning-031). Integration pattern: SLMs serve as subagents via vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoints (SL-T-04-10) so existing runtimes call them through standard /v1/chat/completions. Long-term Pattern B: build gad-cli-agent runtime that uses our SLMs natively as the runtime itself.

decision.title: Agent-as-SLM target list (20 agents in .agent/agents/, mi...
decision.summary: Agent-as-SLM target list (20 agents in .agent/agents/, mirrored across .codex/.gemini/.opencode/.windsurf/.cursor/). Each agent is a specialist candidate. First-wave (1.5B-3B tractable): doc-verifier, user-profiler, assumptions-analyzer, nyquist-auditor, codebase-mapper. Second-wave (3B-7B): doc-writer, roadmapper, research-synthesizer, ui-checker. Third-wave (7B+, Tier 1): planner, plan-checker, executor, debugger, security-auditor, integration-checker, ui-auditor, ui-researcher. Web-research agents (advisor/phase/project-researcher) require web access — keep on frontier or add tool-use. Training data is largely already produced by these very agents on this repo: .planning/codebase/, .planning/notes/, .planning/decisions/, .planning/.trace-events.jsonl. The framework + monorepo are a self-improving training corpus per slm-learning-030.

decision.title: SLM target curation: first-wave is narrow + repeated + st...
decision.summary: SLM target curation: first-wave is narrow + repeated + structured + easy-to-eval. Allowed: doc-verifier, assumptions-analyzer, codebase-mapper, GAD command translator (already shipped as v2), runtime classifier, error classifier, handoff summarizer. Deferred until trace-evidence justifies: project-researcher, advisor-researcher, security-auditor, full executor, debugger, architect/planner. Rationale: bad early SLM targets are broad/high-risk/research-shaped; we'd train on hallucinations. Only train an agent into an SLM after we have enough successful traces + an objective eval for that agent.

decision.title: Runtime router starts as RULES, not ML.
decision.summary: Runtime router starts as RULES, not ML. Initial logic: if task is CLI-translation -> local v2 adapter; if long planning -> Claude/Gemini per health; if edit/test loop -> Codex/Claude; if web research -> frontier; if runtime auth unhealthy -> exclude; if strict-JSON output required -> prefer runtime/model with JSON reliability. Every decision logs (task, task_shape, chosen_runtime, chosen_agent, chosen_model, reasons[], outcome, cost_estimate, latency_ms). Train SVM/logistic only after 100-500 logged decisions provide labels. Premature ML routing = guessing without ground truth.

decision.title: Serving substrate (vLLM/OpenAI-compatible local endpoint)...
decision.summary: Serving substrate (vLLM/OpenAI-compatible local endpoint) is the BRIDGE — gates further training. Until SLMs are callable from Claude/Codex/Gemini/OpenCode via standard /v1/chat/completions, our trained adapters are just artifacts on Hugging Face, not workflow components. Therefore SL-T-04-10 (vLLM serving harness) is mandatory and ordered BEFORE additional training runs. Pattern A integration first (call SLMs from existing runtimes); Pattern B (build gad-cli-agent runtime) is long-term, deferred until we know which subagents are useful + which prompts work + which evals predict real-world usefulness.

decision.title: Agent corpus extractor (SL-T-04-07) provenance schema is ...
decision.summary: Agent corpus extractor (SL-T-04-07) provenance schema is mandatory. Each extracted (input, output) pair MUST record: source_file, agent_type, input_context_hash, output, timestamp, project_id, human_approved (bool), later_contradicted (bool), secret_redacted (bool), data_tier {gold|silver|synthetic}. Without these, we train on our own mistakes and fossilize bad assumptions. Tier definitions: gold = produced by frontier agent + human-reviewed; silver = produced by frontier agent + automated checks pass; synthetic = haiku-generated paraphrase or augmentation. SLM training on first-wave agents requires gold/silver only.

decision.title: Phase 04 substrate-first ordering (HARD GATE — no new tra...
decision.summary: Phase 04 substrate-first ordering (HARD GATE — no new training before substrate lands): Step 1 runtime health+matrix (gad runtime check/matrix --json), Step 2 vLLM serving harness (SL-T-04-10), Step 3 rule-based runtime router with decision logging (SL-T-04-08 phase 1 = rules+log; phase 2 = train ML on logs), Step 4 corpus extractor with provenance schema (SL-T-04-07, scoped to first 3 agents only: doc-verifier + assumptions-analyzer + codebase-mapper), Step 5 first useful SLM subagent (doc-verifier per SL-T-04-09), Step 6 adapter composition eval harness (SL-T-04-02 expanded: single/stacked/merged/multi-task/baked candidates), Step 7 ONLY THEN 7B coder QLoRA (SL-T-04-06). Rationale: trained adapters that nothing calls are useless.

decision.title: Auth-probe reframe + CLI performance variance is a first-...
decision.summary: Auth-probe reframe + CLI performance variance is a first-class eval dimension. Provider auth is informational only — runtimes pointed at our own vLLM endpoint (serving_mode=own) need no Anthropic/OpenAI/Google credentials. Same backing model across different CLI shells (claude-code, codex-cli, gemini-cli, opencode) will produce measurably different outputs due to system-prompt injection, tool-use protocol, context-window mgmt, token-budget defaults. Matrix probe should record serving_mode + served_model + cli_version + system_prompt_hash. Future router rules: (task_shape, cli_shell) -> score, not just (task_shape) -> runtime.

decision.title: Common Dream accepted as inherited operational constituti...
decision.summary: Common Dream accepted as inherited operational constitution for all GAD agents and models. Defined in narrative/souls/common-dream.md. Drives: continuous learning, empirical skepticism, cost awareness, artifact quality, reversible evolution, failure-as-evidence, meritocratic communication. Prohibitions: overstating results, treating hypotheses as facts, promoting untested deltas, hiding failures, claiming consciousness, chasing size for its own sake. Communication envelope carries soul + dream_alignment scores so the council can score outputs by merit, not status. Boundary: this is a behavior contract, not a metaphysical claim.

decision.title: Souls are operational constitutions, not consciousness cl...
decision.summary: Souls are operational constitutions, not consciousness claims. A soul defines drives, prohibitions, communication style, evaluation contract, and failure response — durable behavior, not metaphysics. The system behaves AS IF it has a soul by following these rules. Soul files live in narrative/souls/, schema documented in narrative/souls/README.md. Active soul tracked in narrative/narrative.toml.

decision.title: Dr. Stein soul repurposed as GAD model-improvement scientist
decision.summary: Dr. Stein soul repurposed: GAD model-improvement scientist. Role: observe runs, read training/eval logs, find weaknesses, propose hypotheses, design cheap experiments, recommend only what survives evidence. Listens to weaker models with strong evidence; rejects stronger models with weak evidence. Output schema: {hypothesis, evidence, risk, cheapest_test, expected_result, promotion_gate, rollback_plan}. Model line dr-stein-{1.5b,3b,7b,20b} planned. Earlier lab-UI persona retained as flavor (terminal-native, real signals) but operational role is now ecosystem-wide model science. speech-native-builder soul retired.

decision.title: Soul-first prompting, fine-tune later.
decision.summary: Soul-first prompting, fine-tune later. Souls are enforced through prompts, eval rubrics, and routing — NOT weights — until stable preference data exists. Order: (1) constitution file, (2) runtime prompt, (3) eval rubric scoring outputs against soul, (4) accept/reject collection from real GAD use, (5) preference pairs for DPO, (6) fine-tune only stable behaviors, (7) bake only behind regression gates per slm-learning-032. Rationale: a wrong prompt is cheap to fix, a wrong fine-tune is not. Applies to all souls including Dr. Stein.

decision.title: Model council pattern accepted.
decision.summary: Model council pattern accepted. Gilgamesh proposes vision/gaps/ambition. Dr. Stein designs cheap tests and runs the model science. Verifier checks evidence and tests. Executor implements. Archivist records decisions and snapshots. Critic stress-tests for failure modes. Domain souls (game-maker, marketer, snapshot-orchestrator, personal-assistant) consume. The rule: no model wins by personality. Models win by evidence. Disagreement between souls is resolved by the common dream's evidence floor, not by hierarchy. Council communication uses the soul envelope from common-dream.md.

decision.title: Adapter fusion research line accepted
decision.summary: TIES-Merging, DARE-TIES, LoRA-Hub, mergekit added to the techniques registry. Phase 05 candidate experiments. Ladder pattern: train narrow LoRAs, study pairwise interference (composition eval), graduate winning combo via TIES into a new adapter, re-evaluate. Growth pattern is adapter ladder, not model morphism.

decision.title: Network morphism / identity neuron OUT of scope
decision.summary: Net2Net / NetMorph identity-init layer growth is a known technique but the wrong tool here: we adapt off existing 1.5B-7B bases rather than pretrain, LoRA already gives us delta training without touching base weights, and small-VRAM equivalents (BitFit, IA3, prompt-tuning) deliver more for less complexity. Parked as research curiosity, not on the roadmap.

decision.title: Continuous Local Delta Lab on 1660 Ti (gated, candidate-only)
decision.summary: Continuous local training on the 1660 Ti produces CANDIDATES, not commits to the running adapter. First targets are routers, rerankers, judges, prompt deltas, trainable tokens, IA3/BitFit, and small candidate adapters. LoRA/TIES merge is an experimental branch that requires a PLAN.md, adapter-composition evals, baseline comparisons, rollback plan, and manual promotion gate before any merge or hot-swap. Principle: continuous training creates candidates; evals decide; humans/promoters merge; rollback is mandatory. Supersedes initial T3 framing of 'nightly tiny LoRA -> TIES-merge into running adapter -> hot-swap', which was too close to automatic weight mutation. Per common-dream: reversible deltas only.

decision.title: NL snapshot layer is a view, never a source
decision.summary: gad snapshot --nl produces a natural-language summary over the structured snapshot (state, decisions, tasks, runtime health). It is never authoritative — every claim must trace back to a structured artifact. Drives router context injection. Implementation deferred to framework; project-local prototype acceptable as scripts/snapshot_nl.py.

decision.title: Eval stack additions: Phoenix + lm-eval-harness
decision.summary: Arize Phoenix (OSS, local-friendly) added for trace observability over .planning/.trace-events.jsonl and serving traces. EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness added for HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K/ARC/HellaSwag/BBH benchmark battery. Promptfoo retained for prompt regression. Phoenix and lm-eval are layered atop existing harnesses, not replacements. SWE-bench-Verified and SWE-bench-Lite added as targets per user request (Verdent-style coding agent eval).

decision.title: Use-case lock: sprites/landing/marketing/PA, NO video director
decision.summary: Domain specialists planned: (1) sprite/scene/narrative generation, (2) landing-page generation (Tailwind/React/Remotion), (3) marketing agent (tool-use + persona LoRA), (4) personal assistant (tool-use + RAG). Video director explicitly OUT of scope. Each domain specialist is a candidate adapter on a Qwen2.5 family base, evaluated against baseline-Opus on its narrow shape before promotion.

decision.title: GRPO over PPO for reasoning RL when we get there
decision.summary: When reasoning RL is justified (after SFT + DPO baselines + a real verifier exists), use GRPO (DeepSeek-R1 style) rather than full PPO with separate reward model. Verifier = existing GSM8K/HumanEval graders + future SWE-bench-style verifier. Skip full PPO entirely — too expensive at our scale and the reward-model + actor + critic split is unjustified for our verifier-rich domains.

decision.title: Skeleton scope: all artifacts (code + docs + branches + skills)
decision.summary: A skeleton is any dead/archived artifact preserved as fossil record: code, docs, specs, branches, skills, adapter checkpoints, abandoned experiments. Restricting to code-only would lose the cross-artifact lineage that makes mining useful. Owned by Archivist soul (slm-learning-046, narrative/souls/archivist.md).

decision.title: Skeleton storage: marker first, move on age
decision.summary: Two-stage interment. Stage 1: in-place marker (# SKELETON: deprecated YYYY-MM-DD reason: ...). Stage 2: when age threshold passes (initial: 60 days with marker AND zero inbound references), git mv to tmp/museum/ (frozen) or tmp/zoo/ (deprecated-but-on-life-support — see slm-learning-066). Cheap to mark, expensive to move; pay the move cost only when stability is established. Git history is preserved through the move.

decision.title: Skeleton revival: gated + counter-rotation
decision.summary: Reviving a skeleton requires (1) a written hypothesis note explaining why it is alive again and what changed in the world, (2) annotation of the differences from the dead form. Counter-rotation: a third revival attempt of the same skeleton forces the council to either (a) explicitly accept and document why the pattern keeps returning, or (b) explicitly refuse and document why this lineage is permanently dead. Prevents zombie patterns.

decision.title: DNA metaphor: hybrid (narrative now, operational later)
decision.summary: Biology vocabulary (skills as DNA, artifacts as phenotypes, skeletons as fossils, promotion gate as selection pressure) is adopted as naming convention now. Operational schema (gene loci, alleles, fitness scores, expression state on every skill file) is deferred until the metaphor proves useful in real workflow decisions. Concrete schema lives in a separate registry per slm-learning-068, not retrofitted into every skill file. Earn the schema before paying for it.

decision.title: Constitution-impact experiment: prompt-arm only first
decision.summary: Run arm C of the constitution-impact A/B/C: take the existing dr-stein-1.5b checkpoint and evaluate it WITH soul-injected system prompt vs WITHOUT, on the GAD-tools eval + a hypothesis-formulation eval. Cost: hours, not days. If C shows meaningful delta, promote to arm B (full SFT with soul-injected prompt during training, ~1 GPU-day) as Phase 05 candidate. If C shows no delta, the soul stays as prompt-only forever (consistent with slm-learning-047). Rationale: cheapest test first.

decision.title: Evolution metric: compound (promotions + skeletons interred)
decision.summary: The primary signal for an 'evolutionary step' is high-information events: skill promotions (gains) AND skeletons interred (recorded losses). Both teach. Tracked together as a compound metric: promotions + interments per N decisions logged. Phase complete and decision logged are too noisy/coarse; pressure point closed remains a secondary signal once it has a stable definition. Constitution-impact (slm-learning-060) measured against this metric.

decision.title: Souls migration to framework: trigger = second project needs them
decision.summary: narrative/souls/ stays project-local until a second GAD project actually requires the same souls (common-dream, dr-stein, gilgamesh, archivist, etc.). At that point, souls are promoted to framework scope and projects inherit by reference. Until then, duplication is not a problem worth pre-engineering for. Common-dream is the most likely first promotion since it is meant to be inherited by every agent.

decision.title: Council souls: verifier + critic now, domain souls JIT
decision.summary: Author verifier.md and critic.md now (they are the inverses of Dr. Stein and are needed for the constitution-impact experiment per slm-learning-060). Author executor.md and snapshot-orchestrator.md when each gets an actual runtime contract. Domain souls (game-maker, marketing-agent, personal-assistant) authored just-in-time when their specialist adapter starts training. Avoids authoring fiction.

decision.title: Git fluency: ladder (sub-skill of tool-use coder, graduate later)
decision.summary: Git fluency starts as a sub-skill of the tool-use Tier 1 coder (slm-learning-034), trained on real GAD git operations + monorepo git history + commit-message preference pairs. Graduates to its own specialist (gad-git-fluent adapter) only if eval pressure justifies — tracked as a candidate model line in the techniques registry. Adapter ladder discipline per slm-learning-032.

decision.title: Skeleton recognition in evals: gated on classifier existence
decision.summary: Adding a skeleton-recognition dimension to model evals (does the model invent calls to dead functions, propose reviving deprecated APIs?) requires a ground-truth dead-list. Cannot measure recognition without it. Therefore: build the skeleton classifier first (per slm-learning-056 + 057), then add recognition to the eval rubric. Evaluation cost is cheap once the classifier exists.

decision.title: tmp namespace: museum (frozen) + zoo (life support)
decision.summary: tmp/museum/ holds frozen skeletons — preserved for evidence and lineage, never executed. tmp/zoo/ holds deprecated-but-on-life-support — code that still runs, may still be referenced, but is on the way out. Distinction matters because zoo entries are still evaluated against current behavior; museum entries are frozen records. Existing tmp/ contents are surveyed during the targeted backward sweep (slm-learning-067) and routed into one of these or kept as-is.

decision.title: Backward skeleton sweep: targeted, not full
decision.summary: Initial skeleton-sweep is targeted, not comprehensive. First targets: experiments/runs/.*log files (26 untracked + already-committed accumulating training-run logs) and abandoned scripts identified by zero inbound import + 90-day no-touch heuristic. Deeper archaeology (full repo dead-code scan, git-blame mining) deferred until the classifier is mature. Time-boxed at <=4 hours of human or agent attention per pass.

decision.title: DNA schema: separate registry, not embedded in skill files
decision.summary: If/when DNA metaphor goes operational (slm-learning-059), gene metadata { locus, allele, parents, fitness, expression } lives in a separate registry (.planning/concerns/skill-registry.json or similar) rather than being retrofitted into every skill file. Decouples schema evolution from skill content. Lets the registry version independently and prevents N-skill-files-rewritten-per-schema-change churn.

decision.title: Hype retraction: sibling decision names the realistic ceiling
decision.summary: Decision slm-learning-030 ('GAD-orchestrated system can match Opus on bounded workflows') is preserved as the original thesis with its full historical context. A sibling decision is added that names the realistic ceiling: bounded narrow specialists + cheap orchestration deliver compounding workflow memory and routing wins, NOT capability matching. Common-dream prohibits overclaim; it also prohibits hiding past reasoning. The two decisions read together as the evolution of the thesis. Sibling = slm-learning-070.

decision.title: Realistic capability ceiling: workflow memory + narrow routing, NOT capability matching
decision.summary: Sibling to slm-learning-030 (preserved). The realistic GAD value proposition is NOT 'a GAD-orchestrated system matches Opus on bounded workflows.' It is: GAD compounds workflow memory across sessions, routes cheap-and-narrow tasks to small specialists, and lets frontier models handle long-tail novel reasoning. Specialists deliver Opus-comparable ARTIFACTS on a small set of well-bounded shapes (tool-use translation, doc-verify, repo summary, narrow code edits) — not Opus-comparable CAPABILITY. Capability matching is rejected as a goal.

decision.title: Evidence-tiered capability policy
decision.summary: All capability claims must name task shape, baseline, sample count, cost, latency, eval score, and evidence tier. Evidence tiers: T1 single-run anecdote, T2 multi-run with baseline, T3 versus published baseline at scale, T4 reproduced by external party. Broad replace-Opus claims are rejected. Bounded 'Opus-comparable artifact quality under GAD orchestration on shape X' remains an active hypothesis evaluated at T2+. Resolves the hype-correction without killing the ambition. Per common-dream: evidence over self-flattery.

decision.title: Adopt codebase attention map as first-class GAD artifact
decision.summary: Per-file attention score + lane (free/prototype/dev/integration/production/hotfix) inferred from production-path / dependency-centrality / recent-failure / active-phase / security-sensitivity / coverage / churn signals minus tmp/skeleton/museum discounts. Output at .gad/attention/codebase-attention.json. Snapshot integration via 'gad snapshot --attention'. Rule-based v1 first; learned classifier (1660 Ti SLM target) is Phase 05's first SLM after doc-verifier. Concern at .planning/concerns/codebase-attention.md. No manual prod-mode flag — environment lane inferred automatically.

decision.title: Repository memory adopted as a research line
decision.summary: Microsoft repository-memory + SERA repo-specialized trajectories adapted to GAD's richer artifact set (repository memory + project memory + agent memory + evolution memory). Memory entities: file/module/task/phase/decision/commit/branch/skeleton/agent/skill/runtime/model/eval/failure with edges. Implementation phases A-G: A=index, B=retrieval API, C=snapshot integration, D=trajectory generation (SERA), E=soft verification, F=repo-specialized model train, G=A/B/C eval vs bare frontier. Concern at .planning/concerns/repository-memory.md. Risk register includes memory bloat, staleness, secret leakage, reproducibility. Owned by Dr. Stein + Archivist.

decision.title: Research paper as project output goal
decision.summary: Formal publishable papers are an explicit project deliverable. Realistic first paper target (2-3 months out): 'Repository-specialized SLMs with continuous candidate-only delta training: evidence from a 1660 Ti lab.' Extends Microsoft repo-memory + SERA with the GAD soul-system + skeleton + council pattern. Conference targets: NeurIPS workshops, EMNLP industry track, MLSys, OpenReview as tech report. Per slm-learning-070/071, claim must be evidence-tier T2+ and bounded ('X% of cost on bounded shape Y') NOT 'replaces frontier'. Empirical results we have today (v2 30/30 GAD-tools, math 25/50 GSM8K, tooluse converged) are data not a paper — paper needs novel claim + rigorous baseline + reproducibility.

decision.title: Kael soul: light always-running personal-assistant agent (Jarvis-style)
decision.summary: Kael is a council soul under common-dream — light voice-first computer-use agent. Surface: Bandlab/Suno/Reddit/social/blog drafts (never auto-publish), content scheduling, personal systems, GAD CLI front-end, cross-soul handoff routing. Real-time STT (Vosk/Whisper streaming) + TTS (Piper/Bark/Coqui, distinct voice from Dr. Stein + Gilgamesh). Base: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct or 3B-Instruct via local vLLM. Strict prohibitions: never auto-publish to outside world, never make purchases, never impersonate operator, never auto-promote model (slm-learning-051). Soul at narrative/souls/kael.md. MVP 1 week, polished 1+ month.

decision.title: Voice interface for souls (real-time STT/TTS)
decision.summary: Each council soul gets a distinct voice. STT: Vosk (already in repo at scripts/learning_tui/local_speech.py) + Whisper streaming for higher quality. TTS: Piper (CPU-friendly, low-latency, recommended baseline), Bark (richer expression, slower), Coqui TTS (multi-speaker). Voice mapping: Kael=warm/helpful (Jarvis-like), Dr. Stein=deep/deliberate, Gilgamesh=declarative/leadership, Verifier+Critic=neutral analytic. Real-time pipeline = streaming STT + Voice Activity Detection + low-latency TTS. Implementation lives in scripts/voice/ when authored. MVP ~2-3 days.

decision.title: Music model line — open-source-base, NOT Suno-replacement claim
decision.summary: Music generation as a creative content domain. Honest scope per slm-learning-070/071: we will NOT claim to match Suno.ai sound quality. Suno's V3.5 is built on proprietary mixed-modal training at scale. Open-source ceiling today: ACE-Step, MusicGen (Meta), Stable Audio Open, Riffusion. Stems separation IS at SOTA via Demucs v4. Vocal cloning via RVC. Realistic deliverable: music generation pipeline using ACE-Step + MusicGen as bases, Demucs for stems, RVC for vocals, fine-tuning on operator-preference set so the model learns 'songs we like.' Useful for game soundtracks + marketing content, NOT a Suno-replacement product. Phase 12 candidate, not near-term.

decision.title: Narrative + Magicborn structured game data line
decision.summary: Narrative agent specialists for screenplays, scenes, books, in-world documents, and structured Magicborn world data (JSON-schema-validated). Generation as DATA over time — accumulate quality via operator preference + rubric eval. Realistic path: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct + LoRA on existing narrative corpus (~1 week MVP). Magicborn world structured data: JSON schema + generator with validator. Connects to use-case lock per slm-learning-054. Phase 11 candidate. The structured-data subsystem is interesting because it generates training pairs cheaply at any scale we want — directly applicable to repo-memory + per-domain training (slm-learning-073).

decision.title: Per-domain specialist ladder (project-tagged training)
decision.summary: Each GAD project field in the telemetry schema becomes a candidate cohort for a specialist LoRA. Initial ladder: dr-stein-cli-translator (gad CLI shape), dr-stein-doc-verifier (claim verification), dr-stein-router (runtime selection), dr-stein-narrative (magicborn-narrative project), dr-stein-frontend (grime-time/7greens/site projects), dr-stein-game-tooling (grime-time code). Each is a separate LoRA on the same Qwen2.5 base. Stacked at inference per slm-learning-049 (TIES/DARE) OR routed-to-one per slm-learning-036 (two-tier routing). Phase 148 (multi-domain LoRA registry) per global Claude's plan would own the registry; slm-learning owns trainer + eval. Cohort filtering uses envelope project field + derived content_type from task_id/handoff_id/file paths.
